facts.statement: Matanas enrighti is an extinct duck that lived in New Zealand during the Miocene epoch.
facts.quote: Matanas enrighti is an extinct duck from the Miocene of New Zealand.

facts.statement: The species was described based on a left humerus fossil found at the Saint Bathans Fauna site near Mata Creek in the Central Otago region of New Zealand's South Island.
facts.quote: It was described from fossil material (a left humerus) collected from a Saint Bathans Fauna site near Mata Creek, in the lower Bannockburn Formation of the Manuherikia Group, in the Manuherikia River valley in the Central Otago region of the South Island.

facts.statement: The fossil material used to describe the species was collected from the lower Bannockburn Formation of the Manuherikia Group.
facts.quote: It was described from fossil material (a left humerus) collected from a Saint Bathans Fauna site near Mata Creek, in the lower Bannockburn Formation of the Manuherikia Group, in the Manuherikia River valley in the Central Otago region of the South Island.

facts.statement: The specific epithet enrighti honors Jack Enright, the owner of the station where the type material was collected.
facts.quote: The specific epithet honours Jack Enright, owner of the station on which the type material was collected.

facts.statement: Matanas belongs to the subfamily Anatini.
Matanas is classified within the family Anatidae.
Matanas lived between 18.7 and 15.9 million years ago, spanning the Burdigalian and Langhian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Burdigalian to Langhian (18.7 to 15.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The species was described by Worthy and colleagues in 2007.

rejected.statement: The genus name Matanas combines the name of Mata Creek with the Greek word for duck, anas.
rejected.quote: The genus name is a combination of the name of Mata Creek with anas (duck).
